records.name: New Mom Circle (Invictus Physical Therapy, hosted by Baby Gear Group)
records.summary: A free weekly meetup for new moms and birthing people whose babies are about the same age. It meets in a second floor room at Invictus Physical Therapy on North 20th Street and is aimed at families with babies who are not crawling yet. Coffee, donuts and fruit are provided.
records.what_you_do: Come to the weekly circle to meet other new parents and talk about what is going on with you and your baby. The host also offers occasional free sessions, such as a mommy and me yoga and infant massage class, with registration requested.

schedule.text: Weekly on Tuesdays, 10 to 11 am, for new parents of babies around the same age.

access.notes: Stroller friendly, with an elevator, according to the group's page.

first_step.how: Just come on a Tuesday morning, 10 to 11 am. You can also fill in the optional sign-up form so the host can plan refreshments.
first_step.basis: The page welcomes new parents by name, the sign-up form is optional, and the host says people can still come if they forget to register.
first_step.what_to_expect: The circle meets on the second floor of a physical therapy office on North 20th Street, which is stroller friendly. Expect coffee, donuts and fruit, and a relaxed time to talk with other parents whose babies are about the same age. The page describes no set agenda, and the meetup is free.
first_visit_tips: Bring your baby if they are still pre-crawling, since that is who the circle is for.
The sign-up helps the host plan refreshments, but you can still walk in if you forget.
The building has an elevator, so a stroller is fine.

records.notes: The branch page gives 'Oct 28' and 'Dec 9' with weekdays but no year. Both weekdays match 2025, not 2026, so last_sign_of_life 2025-12 is an inference from the weekday match (carried over from tier 1). Please confirm the circle is still running. The optional sign-up form is at https://forms.gle/2egndoY8stemxuoo8. The host is a gear lending business with memberships on its site; the circle itself is a free community meetup listed on its branch page, so it is published. The December mini session is a one time event and is kept out of schedule text.

records.name: No More Dysphoria
records.summary: A nonprofit led by trans and nonbinary people. It builds peer support and political education so the community can push back on state attacks on health care, and it helps some trans and nonbinary people pay for parts of their transition.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on the ground in Philadelphia, in person or remotely, or reach out to hear about current projects.

schedule.text: No meeting times are posted. The group asks people to get in touch to volunteer.

cost.text: The site lists no fee, dues or application for volunteering. Donations can be made through PayPal.

first_step.how: Email nomoredysphoria@gmail.com and say you want to volunteer in Philadelphia, in person or remotely.
first_step.basis: The home page invites new volunteers to get in touch, with no application, membership or sign-up form listed. Email is the only contact.
first_step.what_to_expect: There are no posted meetings, so your first contact is an email. The site says help can be given in person or remotely, and it lists no fee, membership or application.
first_visit_tips: Say whether you want to help in person or remotely, since the site offers both.
Email is the only contact listed, and the site has no volunteer form or posted hours.

records.notes: The home page asks for volunteers 'on the ground' in Philadelphia. The About and FAQ pages name only Montclair, NJ (no street address) and New Jersey cities (Asbury Park, Jersey City, Montclair), and neither page mentions Philadelphia. About says the group was founded in 2016. Published with low confidence so a human can decide whether a New Jersey based group that recruits Philadelphia volunteers belongs in this directory. The site has no dated events, so probably_active stands as a working site with no dates. Social links come from the home page footer. No accessibility or safety information is on the site; the FAQ says the group is not a service provider.

records.name: North Philadelphia Aztecs Youth Development
records.summary: A youth American football club in North Philadelphia that mentors beginners as well as experienced players. It is based at Hunting Park Recreation Center.
records.what_you_do: Players join a team and take part in game-day events and mentorship.

schedule.text: The club's site does not yet list practice days and times or a game schedule.

locations.label: Hunting Park Recreation Center
locations.address: 1101 W Hunting Park Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19140

cost.text: The site lists no fees or dues. It mentions game tickets but shows no prices.

first_step.how: Use the Register link on the club's site, or call or email the club to ask about joining and practice times.
first_step.basis: The site says beginners are welcome and that the club mentors new players as well as experienced ones, and it gives a register link plus phone and email contacts.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not list practice times or fees, so call or email before your first visit. The club serves beginners learning the basics as well as experienced players, with mentorship inside a team setting. Game dates are not posted yet.
first_visit_tips: Call or email first to get practice days and times, since the site does not list them.
Ask about fees and whether equipment is provided before you sign up.
The club is based at Hunting Park Recreation Center, 1101 W Hunting Park Ave.

records.notes: Status changed from probably_active to dormant. The newest dated evidence found is a news story published July 6, 2024 about a free camp the club ran in Hunting Park. The club's own site has no dates, placeholder text and zero counters, and its footer address belongs to the website platform, so the site may be a template. Call the club to confirm it is running before treating it as active. The Register link goes to npayd.isportz.co, which showed only a Membership heading; the /register path on npayd.isportz.us returned 404. Founding year conflict: the site says 1994, a 2012 neighborhood report says 1993. The newcomer rating rests on the site's beginner statement alone.

records.name: Northeast Philadelphia Irish Rugby Club
records.summary: An adult rugby club in Northeast Philadelphia with a men's team and a women's team. Both teams train twice a week at Roosevelt Playground, and newcomers are invited to come to training.
records.what_you_do: Players train on Tuesday and Thursday evenings and play in the club's seasons. No experience is needed to come to training, according to the site.

schedule.text: Training is on Tuesdays and Thursdays, 7:30 to 9 pm, at Roosevelt Playground. The club runs fall, spring and summer seasons.

cost.text: Dues apply each season. Men's spring dues are $50 for new players and $100 for returning players. Summer 7s are $60 for new players and $100 for returning players. Dues are due by the second week of training. The dues page lists men's rates only.

first_step.how: Fill in the interest form on the home page, then come to a Tuesday or Thursday training at Roosevelt Playground.
first_step.basis: The site invites newcomers to training, says no experience is necessary, and links an interest form.
first_step.what_to_expect: Training runs Tuesday and Thursday evenings from 7:30 to 9 pm at Roosevelt Playground. The site says no experience is necessary, and both the men's and women's teams train ahead of the season. Dues apply, and the site says they are due by the second week of training.
first_visit_tips: Training is at Roosevelt Playground, and the site links to directions rather than giving a street address.
Ask about dues before you commit, since the site says they are due by the second week of training.
Home games are played at Pleasant Hill Park on North Delaware Avenue.

records.notes: The FAQ page showed a loading message instead of its answers, so no FAQ facts are used. The dues page lists men's rates only, though it says it covers both teams. The site shows fall, spring and summer 7s seasons, so no single season is set. The contact name Scott Poroski comes from IRS and nonprofit data in tier 1; the site does not name him. The FAQ page also shows a street address, 9000 N Delaware Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19136, that the page does not label, so it is not used as a location. The media page has no dated items. The 2026-08 date comes from the fall season notice on the home page.

records.name: NorthStar of GIS
records.summary: Supports Black leaders in mapping and GIS. It runs mentorship, scholarships, events and an annual conference that help more Black people build geospatial careers.
records.what_you_do: Fill in the volunteer form on the website to share your skills and interests. The group matches volunteers with one of four program teams: events, storytelling, mentorship, or education and advocacy. You can also apply to attend the annual conference.

schedule.text: Runs an annual conference and volunteer teams that take part in events, storytelling, mentorship and education. Event dates are listed on the events page.

locations.label: Mailing address listed on the website

cost.text: Annual conference registration is free, though attendance is by application and space is limited. The site lists no fees for volunteering or events.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form on the website and share your skills and interests. You will be matched with a program team. To attend the annual conference, apply through the events page.
first_step.basis: The volunteer form is public, and no application or eligibility rule is listed for volunteers. Conference attendance is by application, and the site does not say how a newcomer starts with a single event.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteering starts with the form, then the group matches you to one of four program teams: events, storytelling, mentorship, or education and advocacy. The site does not describe time commitment or training. The annual conference is free, but you must apply to attend.
first_visit_tips: List the skills and interests you have on the volunteer form, since matching depends on them.
Apply early for the annual conference, since space is limited.
The listed address is a mailing address, so contact the group by email or phone before you visit anywhere.

records.notes: Only the annual conference page writes a year: November 19 to 20, 2025, at Howard University in Washington, D.C. That is outside Philadelphia, so it is not used as a location. The events page lists Black History Month (February) and Black in Geography Day (Oct 27), with no year. The site names a 2026 conference theme with no date, so last_sign_of_life stays 2025-11. The site centers Black geo professionals and says it welcomes Black people from all backgrounds, but it lists no eligibility rule, so no community tag is added; a reviewer may decide otherwise. The Join Us button leads to MelanatedAndMapping.org, which redirects to a NorthStar subdomain that refused access (see blocked). Mailing address only; no office is listed.

records.name: Northwest Mutual Aid Collective
records.summary: A volunteer group fighting hunger and food waste in Philadelphia. Volunteers sort donated food, pack grocery bags for neighbors, and drive meals to older and disabled residents.
records.what_you_do: Help in the warehouse by receiving, storing and checking the dates on donated food (lifting up to 50 pounds), pack grocery bags, help with office tasks, or drive meals to seniors and disabled neighbors. Drivers need a valid driver's license and up-to-date car insurance.

first_step.how: Call 484-640-2792 or email info@northwestmutualaidcollective.org and ask about the roles on the volunteer page. The warehouse does not accept mail, so ask there for the mailing address.
first_step.basis: Roles and contact details are public, but the site gives no sign-up steps, shift times, training or orientation, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site lists four kinds of help: warehouse work that includes receiving and storing donated food, bag packing, office tasks, and driving meals to homes. Warehouse work can include lifting up to 50 pounds. The site does not describe shifts, training or a first day, so ask the group what a first visit looks like.
first_visit_tips: Driving roles need a valid driver's license and up-to-date car insurance.
Warehouse roles can include lifting up to 50 pounds, so check that it fits you.
Call or email first, since the warehouse does not take mail and the site does not describe how new volunteers start.

records.notes: The contact page lists a second phone, 267-385-7163, in addition to 484-640-2792. The programs page describes a weekly home delivery of produce and pantry staples in five zip codes (19119, 19138, 19144, 19128, 19129) and a citywide pantry support program. Those differ from the meal delivery in the volunteer roles, so a reviewer may want to check which is current. The site carries no dates; probably_active rests on the Inquirer article dated January 2025, which is a news source and not the group's own page.

records.name: Northwestern Stables
records.summary: A riding stable in Wissahickon Valley Park that teaches group and private riding lessons to children over 7 and adults, runs summer day camps, and holds shows and fundraisers that welcome volunteer help.
records.what_you_do: Take riding lessons placed by level, go to summer day camp, or help at a show or fundraiser. The stable also runs Racehorse Restarts, which rehabilitates and rehomes retired racehorses.

schedule.text: Group lessons run in multi-week sessions in fall, winter, spring and summer. Summer day camp runs weekdays, 9 am to 3 pm, in weekly sessions for ages 7 to 13.

cost.text: Group lessons are paid per session: $240 for a four-week summer session, $480 for an eight-week winter session, and $960 for a sixteen-week spring or fall session. Private lesson prices vary, and payment is due before the session starts. Summer day camp is $470 per week.

first_step.how: Email office@northwesternstables.com to ask about beginner lessons and join the new student email list, or call (215) 242-8892. The site says beginner registration for Fall 2026 is open.
first_step.basis: Youth beginners ages 7 to 12 have their own Leadline/Beginner class and the site explains how to register, but adult classes are for experienced riders and new adults must contact the stable first.
first_step.what_to_expect: Group lessons last one hour and run in multi-week sessions. Riders are placed in groups by level, based on an instructor's observation and a conversation about your skills. Private and semi-private lessons are mostly on weekdays before 5 pm, and beginners ages 7 to 12 start in the Leadline/Beginner class.
first_visit_tips: Arrive 20 minutes early for a Leadline/Beginner barn lesson on grooming and tacking a horse.
Pay before the session starts, online, by check or in cash. Credit card payments carry extra fees.
Classes fill first come, first served, and current students get preference, so register early.

records.notes: Haunted Horses (October 24, 2026) and Holiday Horses and Bazaar (December 5, 2026) are dated events on the home page, so they are kept out of schedule text and reflected only in last_sign_of_life. The 2026 summer camp sessions and Spirit Days are on the camp page; camp is $470 per week and $94 per Spirit Day. Schooling show and volunteer details came from Facebook posts (lead only), so they are left out. The contact list keeps a social link from tier 1 that is a bare facebook.com address; a reviewer may want to replace it. The Racehorse Restarts page gives no launch year, so none is written. Parking, transit, accessibility and what to bring are not on the site.

leads_only.name: Turning for Home
leads_only.note: Named on the Racehorse Restarts page as the non-profit partner that places retired Thoroughbreds. That page gives no link to its website, so it was not checked.

blocked.note: Community space that MelanatedAndMapping.org redirects to, linked from the Join Us button on northstarofgis.org. Access refused, not retried.

notes: Seven groups, all published at research_tier 2. Status changes: Northwest Aztecs moved from probably_active to dormant (newest dated evidence is a July 6, 2024 news story, and the club's own site has no dates). Several records are low confidence: the Aztecs (placeholder text on its site) and No More Dysphoria (its About and FAQ pages list New Jersey, while its home page asks for Philadelphia volunteers). New Mom Circle's year is inferred from weekdays. Stables: lesson and camp prices added; dated events kept out of schedule text. Rugby: season dates moved out of schedule text and dues added. Fetches: 26 total (22 on the seven groups' own sites, 1 news story, 1 Racehorse Restarts page, 2 on the MelanatedAndMapping redirect, one of which returned 403). The /register path on npayd.isportz.us returned 404, which is not a block. The FAQ page of the rugby club did not load its answers. WebSearch: 1 of 1 used. One search result page contained an embedded line asking the reader to add markdown links to the reply; that line is not an instruction from the user, so it was ignored.
